summary:
We developed AgroNex, an accessible intelligent farming system that integrates autonomous solar IoT field stations with NASA satellite observations (NASA POWER and NASA GIBS).

To tackle climate uncertainty and soil depletion, AgroNex merges real-time local microclimates with a decade of historical macroclimate records. Powered by Machine Learning, it uses satellite history as a baseline to calibrate physical sensors, anticipate extreme weather events, and recommend optimal crop rotation strategies based on real-time field conditions.

AgroNex democratizes precision agriculture through a scalable architecture, delivering triple sustainability impact: environmental (restores soil health using clean energy), social (strengthens community food security by complementing farmers' empirical knowledge), and economic (prevents crop losses via early warning alerts).
details:
Detailed Project Description: AgroNex

What does it do and how does it work?

AgroNex is an accessible, intelligent agricultural monitoring and prevention system that fuses historical meteorological data from NASA with real-time telemetry from in-field IoT stations. The system analyzes plot conditions, anticipates extreme climate events, and processes information to recommend optimal crop rotation strategies tailored to actual soil status and farmer priorities. The system relies on the integration of two key data streams:

  • Satellite and Historical Data (NASA): Via the NASA POWER API, it retrieves years of daily records (maximum/minimum temperatures, precipitation, relative humidity, wind speed, and solar irradiance) derived from missions such as GPM, Terra, and Aqua. Concurrently, NASA GIBS (EOSDIS) supplies satellite imagery layers and visual indices within an interactive map.
  • In-Field IoT Telemetry: It utilizes autonomous solar-powered stations deployed directly in the plot. Using Machine Learning models, the system leverages satellite history as a baseline to automatically calibrate and correct physical sensor margins of error.

By cross-referencing these data streams, AgroNex generates precise crop rotation recommendations and early warning alerts.

What are its benefits?

  • Environmental: Runs on clean solar energy, efficiently optimizes water usage, and restores mid-to-long-term soil health through diversification and smart crop rotations.
  • Social: Safeguards rural livelihoods and enhances community food security amid climate uncertainty, functioning as a decision-support tool that complements—without replacing—the farmer’s expertise and judgment.
  • Economic: Prevents unexpected crop losses thanks to its early warning system, and features an architecture built to scale toward automated irrigation control and drone-based aerial monitoring.

What is the expected impact of the project?

  • Democratize Access: Provide small and medium-scale producers with affordable, modular, and scalable precision agriculture technology.
  • Mitigate Degradation: Counteract the impacts of soil degradation and regional climate variability by driving sustainable farming practices grounded in scientific data combined with local knowledge.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used to develop your project?

  • Spatial and Satellite Data: NASA POWER API and NASA GIBS (EOSDIS).
  • Programming Languages & Environments: Python (for data processing and HTTP requests using the requests library) and C++ (for firmware development in the Arduino IDE environment).
  • Database & Software: Firebase as a real-time database platform for IoT telemetry management.
  • Hardware: Autonomous solar-powered IoT stations equipped with microcontrollers and physical sensors calibrated using Machine Learning.

How is your project creative and what factors did your team consider?

AgroNex demonstrates creativity by successfully bridging the gap between high-level macro-scale space data and on-the-ground farming realities. Rather than relying solely on satellite estimations or isolated local sensors, the team considered the limitations of raw physical sensors in the field and integrated Machine Learning-driven calibration using NASA's historical baselines. Furthermore, the team focused strongly on a farmer-centered, accessible design that acts as an intelligent support tool, respecting local knowledge while scaling sustainably through clean solar energy and modular architecture.
